Group Chief Financial Officer (Group CFO)

About the Role

We are seeking an accomplished and strategically minded Group Chief Financial Officer (Group CFO) to lead the financial strategy, performance, capital management, investment finance, and financial governance of a diversified Insurance & Investments Group.

The Group CFO will have enterprise-wide responsibility for the Group's financial affairs, overseeing finance across subsidiaries, business units, investment entities, and operating companies.

As a key member of the Group Executive Leadership Team, the Group CFO will serve as a strategic advisor to the Group CEO, President, Board, Investment Committee, and other senior stakeholders, ensuring disciplined capital allocation, strong financial performance, balance-sheet resilience, regulatory compliance, and long-term shareholder value creation.

The role requires a sophisticated financial leader with experience across insurance, investment management, asset management, financial services, corporate finance, capital markets, and regulated financial institutions.

Key Responsibilities

1. Group Financial Strategy & Leadership

Develop and execute the Group's overall financial strategy in alignment with corporate objectives.

Provide strategic financial advice to the Group CEO, President, Board, and Executive Committee.

Establish Group-wide financial policies, standards, controls, and performance frameworks.

Ensure effective financial governance across subsidiaries, business units, joint ventures, and investment entities.

Lead the development of the Group's long-term financial and capital strategy.

2. Group P&L & Financial Performance

Assume overall responsibility for the Group's financial performance, profitability, balance sheet, cash flow, and capital position.

Monitor performance across all subsidiaries and business lines.

Drive sustainable earnings growth, expense efficiency, and return on capital.

Establish Group-wide financial KPIs and performance dashboards.

Challenge business-unit leadership on financial performance and corrective actions.

3. Financial Planning & Performance Management

Lead Group-wide annual budgeting, forecasting, and long-range financial planning.

Develop financial scenarios and stress tests to support strategic decision-making.

Consolidate financial plans across subsidiaries and investment businesses.

Monitor actual performance against budgets, forecasts, and strategic objectives.

Strengthen management reporting and financial analytics.

4. Insurance Finance

Provide executive oversight of financial management across insurance businesses.

Monitor premiums, claims, reserves, expenses, underwriting results, and insurance profitability.

Oversee financial analysis of loss ratios, combined ratios, expense ratios, and underwriting margins.

Partner with actuarial, underwriting, claims, and risk functions to understand financial exposures.

Provide financial input into product profitability, pricing, reinsurance, and portfolio decisions.

5. Investment & Asset Management Finance

Provide Group-level financial oversight of investment portfolios and investment businesses.

Partner with the Chief Investment Officer (CIO) and Investment Committee on investment strategy and performance.

Monitor investment income, portfolio returns, asset allocation, liquidity, and risk-adjusted performance.

Evaluate strategic investment opportunities and major portfolio decisions.

Ensure investment activities support the Group's liabilities, capital objectives, liquidity needs, and risk appetite.

6. Group Capital & Solvency Management

Lead Group-wide capital planning and capital optimization.

Monitor capital adequacy, solvency, leverage, liquidity, and financial resilience.

Develop strategies to optimize capital deployment across subsidiaries and business lines.

Assess the capital implications of acquisitions, investments, dividends, growth initiatives, and strategic transactions.

Partner with Risk and Actuarial leadership on capital and solvency assessments.

7. Asset-Liability Management

Provide executive oversight of asset-liability management (ALM) across relevant insurance and investment businesses.

Ensure investment portfolios are appropriately aligned with insurance liabilities and liquidity requirements.

Monitor duration, interest-rate sensitivity, liquidity gaps, and market exposures.

Support balance-sheet optimization and financial stress-testing initiatives.

8. Treasury & Liquidity

Lead Group treasury, liquidity, cash management, and banking relationships.

Establish Group-wide liquidity policies and funding strategies.

Optimize cash across subsidiaries while maintaining appropriate regulatory and operational liquidity.

Oversee debt facilities, guarantees, intercompany funding, and treasury risk.

Monitor interest-rate, foreign-exchange, credit, and liquidity exposures.

9. Capital Raising & Financing

Lead Group-level financing and capital-raising initiatives.

Develop relationships with banks, institutional investors, private equity firms, development-finance institutions, debt providers, and capital-market participants.

Oversee debt issuance, refinancing, capital injections, and other funding strategies.

Optimize the Group's capital structure and cost of capital.

Ensure funding capacity supports strategic growth.

10. M&A, Investments & Corporate Development

Lead financial evaluation of acquisitions, disposals, strategic investments, and joint ventures.

Oversee financial due diligence, valuation, transaction modeling, and deal structuring.

Assess the impact of transactions on earnings, capital, solvency, liquidity, and shareholder value.

Partner with the CEO and Board on major strategic transactions.

Oversee financial integration and post-transaction performance.

11. Group Financial Reporting & Consolidation

Ensure accurate and timely consolidated financial reporting across the Group.

Oversee statutory accounts, management reporting, regulatory returns, and Board reporting.

Establish consistent accounting and reporting standards across subsidiaries.

Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards and insurance regulations.

Maintain strong relationships with external auditors and professional advisers.

12. Regulatory & Governance

Maintain strong financial governance across the Group.

Ensure compliance with applicable insurance, investment, corporate, tax, and financial regulations.

Manage relationships with regulators, auditors, rating agencies, and other external stakeholders.

Establish effective internal controls and financial policies.

Ensure appropriate governance across subsidiaries, SPVs, joint ventures, and investment entities.

13. Financial Risk Management

Establish and oversee the Group's financial risk-management framework.

Monitor market, credit, liquidity, underwriting, investment, interest-rate, FX, and operational financial risks.

Establish appropriate stress-testing and contingency-planning processes.

Work closely with the Group CRO, Chief Actuary, CIO, and business leaders to manage enterprise-wide risk.

14. Tax Strategy

Oversee Group-wide tax planning, compliance, reporting, and risk management.

Ensure appropriate tax governance across subsidiaries and jurisdictions.

Identify opportunities for legitimate tax efficiency.

Monitor changes in tax and regulatory requirements affecting the Group.

15. Investor & Stakeholder Relations

Develop strong relationships with shareholders, institutional investors, lenders, rating agencies, regulators, and other financial stakeholders.

Lead financial communications to the Board and key investors.

Support investor presentations, annual reports, strategic reviews, and capital-market activities.

Clearly communicate the Group's financial strategy, performance, and outlook.

16. Finance Transformation

Modernize the Group's finance operating model, systems, processes, and reporting infrastructure.

Strengthen ERP, FP&A, consolidation, business intelligence, and financial analytics capabilities.

Drive automation and digital transformation across finance.

Improve transparency and real-time visibility across subsidiaries and business units.

17. Leadership & Organizational Development

Lead the Group Finance function and senior finance leadership across subsidiaries.

Develop a high-performing, commercially focused finance organization.

Establish common standards, talent-development programs, and succession plans.

Build strong relationships with subsidiary CFOs and Finance Directors.

Promote a culture of integrity, accountability, financial discipline, and value creation.

Key Performance Indicators

The Group CFO will be accountable for:

Group revenue and earnings growth

Group EBITDA / net income performance

Return on equity (ROE)

Return on capital

Capital adequacy and solvency

Investment portfolio performance

Investment income and risk-adjusted returns

Candidate Profile

Essential Experience

18+ years of progressive finance experience, including substantial Group or enterprise-level leadership.

Previous experience as Group CFO, CFO, Deputy Group CFO, Group Finance Director, Finance Director, or equivalent.

Significant experience within insurance, investment management, asset management, banking, pensions, reinsurance, or diversified financial services.

Proven experience managing complex group structures, subsidiaries, investment entities, and regulated businesses.

Company: Coherence OS
Location: Remote (Global)
Compensation: Equity-Only (Slicing Pie) → Cash at Break-Even

We’re building Coherence OS because we believe the next era of technology requires more than speed and scale — it requires meaning, integrity, and systems that hold over time.

This role isn’t for someone looking for a job. It’s for someone who wants to build infrastructure they can stand behind years from now, alongside a small, serious team that values fairness, clarity, and real ownership.

We use the Slicing Pie model because it’s the only compensation system we’ve found that actually treats people like adults: contribution in equals ownership earned, dollar for dollar. If that resonates with you — not as a gamble, but as a principle — you’ll probably feel at home here.

About Coherence OS

Coherence OS is an AI-native operating system focused on preserving human meaning, identity, and ethical coherence in the age of advanced automation.

We are building foundational infrastructure intended to support long-lived, global-scale systems — not short-term SaaS experiments.

This role is for someone who wants to build the substrate, not just ship tickets.

Company Stage & Visibility

Coherence OS is in its earliest build phase. We are intentionally operating with a minimal public footprint while core systems, filings, and internal foundations are being finalized.

We do not have a public website yet. Full context about the company, mission, and roadmap will be shared during the interview process.

This role is part of the initial engineering team and is best suited for candidates who are comfortable joining early, helping shape foundational systems, and building before everything is public.

Position

We are seeking a skilled Infrastructure Engineer to design, build, and maintain the infrastructure that powers our applications and services. In this role, you will work closely with engineering, data, and security teams to ensure our systems are scalable, reliable, secure, and highly available.

The ideal candidate has strong experience with cloud platforms, infrastructure automation, and modern DevOps practices, and is passionate about improving system performance and developer productivity.

Responsibilities

Infrastructure Design & Development

  • Design, implement, and maintain scalable cloud infrastructure.
  • Build highly available and fault-tolerant systems.
  • Architect solutions across compute, storage, networking, and security layers.

Infrastructure as Code (IaC)

  • Develop and maintain infrastructure using Terraform.
  • Automate provisioning and configuration of infrastructure environments.
  • Maintain version-controlled infrastructure repositories.

Cloud Platform Management

  • Manage cloud environment - GCP.
  • Optimize infrastructure costs and performance.
  • Implement high-availability and disaster recovery strategies.

CI/CD & Deployment Automation

  • Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for automated deployments.
  • Support containerized application deployments using Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Improve deployment reliability and release processes.

Security & Compliance

  • Implement secure infrastructure practices including IAM, network policies, and access controls.
  • Work with security teams to enforce best practices and compliance standards.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with Kubernetes or container-based platforms.
  • Experience with monitoring tools such as Prometheus, Grafana, or Datadog.
  • Experience with serverless or cloud-native architectures.

raw.description:
Head of Marketing, B2B Growth

If you are a hands-on B2B marketing builder who wants real ownership—not a large inherited team—this is an opportunity to build the marketing engine for an established, growing B2B organization with complementary professional-services and software offerings. You will have meaningful autonomy, a broad mandate, and compensation of $165,000–$200,000 to personally shape the strategy, messaging, campaigns, enablement, measurement, and AI-enabled workflows that help the business scale.

The Opportunity

Our client is an established B2B organization with both relationship-led professional-services revenue and recurring software revenue. The company has grown through strong market relationships and selective marketing support, and now needs one accountable marketing owner to create a more repeatable, measurable, modern growth function.

This is initially a true department-of-one role. You may use contractors or vendors where they create leverage, but this is not a strategy-only executive seat and not a people-management-first role. The right person wants to build the plan, write the copy, shape positioning, launch campaigns, improve systems, and create momentum before every condition is perfect.

The Mandate

You will own marketing across two related but different B2B commercial motions: a relationship-led services business and a software business with recurring revenue dynamics. Success requires commercial judgment, fast learning, strong execution, and the ability to produce credible work quickly in a complex B2B environment.

What You Will Own

  • Build and run a focused marketing plan tied to company goals, revenue priorities, sales needs, campaign opportunities, and measurable progress.
  • Clarify ICPs, buyer problems, positioning, offers, messaging, and channel priorities across professional-services and software motions.
  • Personally create and improve campaigns, landing pages, email, LinkedIn content, thought leadership, case studies, event follow-up, and sales materials.
  • Translate complex B2B topics into clear, credible, buyer-relevant messaging without relying on generic agency output or low-quality AI content.
  • Build a consistent content, campaign, and demand-generation engine that improves shipping velocity, market visibility, and sales usefulness.
  • Partner with senior leaders, sales, product, and subject-matter experts to turn business insight into practical marketing work without becoming a reactive ticket-taker.
  • Improve marketing operations, funnel visibility, reporting, testing, and decision-making from imperfect historical data.
  • Use vendors selectively, rationalize spend, and increase output per dollar while staying personally close enough to the work to raise quality.

What Success Looks Like

In the first year, you will establish a clear marketing plan and operating cadence, create a usable messaging foundation, launch a steady content and campaign rhythm, improve measurement, and build repeatable sales-enablement and event-follow-up motions. The business should see clearer priorities, better marketing throughput, stronger stakeholder trust, and measurable progress in qualified demand, engagement, pipeline influence, or another agreed commercial indicator.

Required Qualifications

  • Substantive B2B marketing experience. This is not a consumer-marketing role.
  • Recent, genuine department-of-one or extremely lean-team ownership where you personally produced and shipped work.
  • Broad experience across demand generation, positioning, content, campaigns, sales enablement, marketing operations, and measurement.
  • Ability to set strategy and execute: you can write, launch, analyze, iterate, and improve the work yourself.
  • Strong copy judgment and the writing ability to make complex B2B topics clear, specific, and commercially useful.
  • Enough visual taste to prevent generic, off-brand, or visibly low-quality output, whether you create assets yourself or direct others.
  • Demonstrable AI-native execution through real workflows, agents, automations, prototypes, campaigns, analysis, or shipped work products—not just familiarity with tools.
  • Comfort creating practical measurement and making decisions despite messy data or incomplete historical reporting.
  • Fast learning, entrepreneurial ownership, prioritization, follow-through, and low-ego partnership with senior stakeholders.
  • Commercial understanding that relationship-led professional-services revenue and recurring software revenue require different marketing motions.
  • Remote United States availability with strong alignment to East Coast working hours.

Preferred Background

Experience marketing both B2B professional services and B2B software is strongly preferred because this role spans two different commercial motions. That said, experience in both is not an automatic knockout if you bring exceptional B2B experience, strong commercial judgment, fast learning, and credible transferable evidence.

Helpful backgrounds may include hands-on Head of Marketing, Director of Marketing, Senior Marketing Manager, Demand Generation, Growth Marketing, or broad B2B marketing ownership in a resource-constrained startup, growth company, professional-services firm, software company, regulated industry, or other complex B2B environment.

AI-Enabled Work Demonstration

Finalists should expect to demonstrate a real AI-enabled marketing workflow they have built or used in practice. The goal is to understand how you research, draft, automate, analyze, validate, and apply judgment—not to reward tool lists or generic prompting language.

Work Model, Travel, and Compensation

  • Remote role for U.S.-based candidates.
  • Strong alignment with East Coast working hours is required.
  • Occasional travel for company meetings, industry events, or conferences may be required.

About Us:

Headquartered in Dallas, Texas, Divcon delivers fully integrated automation solutions nationwide that optimize performance, energy efficiency, and reliability across HVAC, lighting, power monitoring, and mission-critical systems. Leveraging advanced technologies - including Allen-Bradley PLCs, Ignition SCADA, and Delta DDC systems - we combine deep technical expertise with field-tested execution to deliver precise, scalable, and high-performance solutions.

About the role:

The Lead Design Engineer provides advanced technical leadership and oversight for the design, documentation, and implementation of complex building automation and control systems for commercial, industrial, and mission-critical facilities. Building upon the Senior Design Engineer role, this position is responsible for guiding a team of Senior Design Engineers, ensuring engineering excellence, and driving consistency in design standards and execution.

This role serves as a key liaison between engineering leadership and project teams, ensuring high-quality deliverables, alignment with company standards, and continuous improvement of design processes. The Lead Design Engineer plays a critical role in advancing Divcon’s building automation capabilities through leadership, innovation, and cross-functional collaboration.

Key Responsibilities:

Leadership & Team Development

  • Lead, mentor, and provide technical oversight to a team of Senior Design Engineers.
  • Deliver ongoing coaching, performance feedback, and professional development support.
  • Assist the Design Engineering Manager in workload planning, project assignments, and resource allocation.
  • Review and approve design deliverables to ensure technical accuracy, completeness, and compliance.
  • Ensure team adherence to project schedules, milestones, and deliverable timelines.
  • Identify skill gaps and support development of training plans to enhance team capabilities.
  • Drive adoption and enforcement of design standards, templates, and engineering best practices.

Technical Design & Project Execution

  • Lead the design and implementation of DDC control systems across all project phases, including pre-construction, installation, and closeout.
  • Oversee development of HVAC and building automation control system designs, including schematics, riser/network diagrams, panel layouts, and wiring details.
  • Translate mechanical and electrical plans/specifications into complete automation control designs.
  • Develop and review sequences of operation, control narratives, and system logic for complex systems.
  • Prepare and review submittals, bills of material (BOMs), and device specifications.
  • Engineer system architectures utilizing BACnet, Modbus, and IP-based networks.
  • Design and review custom control panels and support FAT/SAT and shop verification activities.
  • Apply NEC, NFPA, ASHRAE, UL, and related codes across all design deliverables.

Quality, Coordination & Continuous Improvement

  • Conduct and oversee QA/QC reviews of drawings, submittals, and as-built documentation.
  • Generate and review RFIs to resolve design clarifications with internal teams and external stakeholders.
  • Coordinate with Project Managers, construction teams, vendors, and customers to ensure project alignment and execution.
  • Support commissioning, troubleshooting, and system startup in collaboration with cross-functional teams.
  • Lead development and refinement of drawing standards, CAD templates, and design workflows.
  • Provide input on product direction, tools, and process improvements in collaboration with engineering leadership.
  • Ensure accurate and timely development of O&M closeout documentation from construction redlines.

Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical, Mechanical, Controls Engineering, or related technical field (or equivalent experience).
  • Strong proficiency in AutoCAD or AutoCAD Electrical for control system design and documentation.
  • Advanced understanding of HVAC systems, control sequences, and DDC integration.
  • In-depth knowledge of control communication protocols (BACnet, Modbus, LonWorks, etc.).
  • Working knowledge of applicable codes: NEC, NFPA, ASHRAE, UL 508A, and local energy codes.
  • Demonstrated leadership, mentoring, or supervisory experience.
  • Excellent organizational, communication, and problem-solving skills.

Experience

  • 7+ years of progressive experience in building automation, MEP design, or industrial controls.
  • Extensive experience designing DDC architectures, system layouts, and control panels.
  • Proven experience reviewing and approving engineering deliverables.
  • Experience supporting commissioning, startup, or system troubleshooting.
  • Prior experience leading teams or overseeing engineering workflows required.
  • PLC/HMI experience (Allen Bradley, Schneider, Siemens) a plus.
  • P.E. or E.I.T. preferred but not required.

Benefits & Total Rewards:

  • Opportunities for Growth

Hands-on training and career advancement in an exploding data-center industry.

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision Insurance

We cover 100% of individual medical premiums and help offset the cost of family coverage.

Eligible after 90 days, with company matching to help you invest in your future.

  • Disability Coverage

Both short- and long-term disability insurance provided at no cost to our employees.

Take time off when you need it, no accruing time necessary.

For eligible field-based roles that require travel, Divcon covers all business travel expenses and provides a per diem, phone allowance, tools, and PPE at no cost. Eligible employees also receive paid training and additional reimbursable business expenses.

raw.description:
CareMind, part of the Mindoula Health family is hiring licensed therapists (LMHC, LCSW, LMFT) to join our fully remote Suicide Prevention & Family Support Program in Washington.

Compensation: For candidates located in Washington State the pay is $90,000 a year. For candidates located outside of Washington, the salary is $75,000 per year plus excellent benefits and the opportunity to work with a fantastic team.

Comprehensive Benefits Package includes:

  • Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance
  • Supplemental Life Insurance
  • Short Term and Long Term Insurance paid by Mindoula
  • 401k, with a company match
  • 3 weeks paid vacation each year, 4 mental wellness days and 11 holidays
  • Parental Leave: 8 weeks of paid parental leave
  • Personal Development Program: $500 credit reimbursement per calendar year

As a Therapist, Suicide Prevention & Family Support (SPFS), you will work in collaborative settings to provide biopsychosocial assessments, individual and group therapy, and work with your team to coordinate care across a range of treatment settings. You will have the ability to manage a caseload and make decisions with appropriate autonomy.

Core Duties:

  • Deliver Family-Centered Psychotherapy: Provide evidence-based individual, joint family, and parent/guardian teletherapy for youth (ages 12–26) at high or critical risk of suicide, utilizing family-systems frameworks, C-CBT, DBT skills, and Motivational Interviewing.
  • Conduct Suicide Risk Assessment & Safety Planning: Administer validated risk assessment tools (e.g., C-SSRS) and lead real-time Safety Planning, lethal means counseling, and crisis stabilization tailored to both the youth and their family unit.
  • Manage Monthly Acuity & Risk Stratification: Complete validated clinical assessments at monthly review periods to measure acuity, track suicide risk trajectory, and dynamically adjust care frequency and treatment goals based on member readiness and family capacity.
  • Lead Clinical Care Team Collaboration: Direct the clinical safety strategy in close partnership with assigned Behavioral Health Support Specialists (BHSS) and the 24/7 crisis response team, ensuring aligned roles without duplicating billable services.
  • Provide Crisis Escalation Response: Serve as the licensed clinician for high-acuity escalations, executing immediate risk mitigation, triage, and rapid safety plan updates during critical member events.
  • Maintain Fee-for-Service & Medicaid Compliance: Complete high-integrity, timely clinical documentation (DAP) that explicitly substantiates medical necessity, suicide risk levels, family interventions, and whole-person care for Medicaid Fee-for-Service (FFS) billing.
  • Drive Multimodal Youth & Family Engagement: Utilize multi-platform engagement technology (video, secure messaging, interactive safety apps) to maintain persistent outreach and re-engage ambivalent youth or overwhelmed caregivers.
  • Integrate Care Infrastructure & Panel Tracking: Actively participate in interdisciplinary huddles, maintain registry accuracy, and monitor personal KPIs (billable hours, documentation turnaround, and show rates) to optimize clinical outcomes across the program panel.
  • Collaborate with the member, family, and healthcare providers to develop an individualized plan of care.
  • Develop and coordinate community resources with emphasis on medical, behavioral, suicide prevention, and social services.
  • Identify and initiate referrals for social service programs – including financial, psycho-social, community, and state supportive services.
  • Document all member assessments, care plans, and referrals provided. Prepare and maintain all required records, reports, paperwork, and member’s diagnostic records, maintaining confidentiality of members at all times.

Skills Required:

  • Relentless about prioritizing and following through on assigned tasks independently. Superior time management and organization to complete daily tasks by the end of each day.
  • Computer proficiency; Including experience with electronic health records (EHR).
  • Ability to exercise strict confidentiality and sound judgment with respect to sensitive member information, maintaining the integrity of member records at all times.
  • Excellent listening, verbal, and written communication skills. Clearly and accurately relay information to staff, business partners, stakeholders, and members including collaborating with interdisciplinary teams (e.g., BHSS).
  • Problem Solving: Identifies needs and takes independent action to implement change when and where it is needed; results oriented. Ability to plan, organize, manage time, and prioritize multiple tasks and assignments.
  • Ability to provide case management in routine and crisis situations.
  • Self-motivated, team player, adaptable with a strong sense of urgency in a fast-paced

Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree in psychology, social work, or other applicable behavioral health discipline from an accredited college or university is required.
  • Licensure: Current Washington Department of Health (WA DOH) independent behavioral health license. Eligible licenses include:
    • Licensed Independent Clinical Social Worker (LICSW)
    • Licensed Mental Health Counselor (LMHC)
    • Licensed Marriage and Family Therapist (LMFT)
  • Two or more years of direct experience working with adolescents and adults in the behavioral health field required. Experience in suicide prevention strongly preferred.
  • Crisis intervention training and experience required.
  • Knowledge of local resources, social determinants of health, mental health, substance use disorders, interpersonal violence, and social issues.
  • Familiarity with Medicare or Medicaid practices preferred

Come be part of the solution!

Salary: $75,000 – $95,000 / year

raw.excerpt: The RoleWe are seeking a hands-on Senior Software Developer / Technical Lead with an AI focus to help us lead teams that build new applications and modernize existing ones for our clients.
raw.description:
The Role

We are seeking a hands-on Senior Software Developer / Technical Lead with an AI focus to help us lead teams that build new applications and modernize existing ones for our clients. You will work as part of an AI Led Application Modernization team that believes the way software is designed, built, tested, and maintained is changing quickly—and that senior technical leaders have an opportunity to shape how teams adopt these changes responsibly and effectively. Among your responsibilities will be:

  1. Set technical direction for delivery teams, including architecture, engineering practices, modernization approach, AI adoption patterns, and quality expectations.
  2. Remain hands-on in the work by designing, coding, reviewing, testing, and troubleshooting software while helping other developers deliver well-architected solutions.
  3. Use AI-assisted development tools and create fit-for-purpose agents and agentic workflows using frameworks such as LangGraph, A2A, MCP-enabled tools, or similar approaches when they are the right solution for a client or delivery challenge.

This role is both hands-on and leadership oriented. You will write code, review AI-generated output, guide architectural decisions, mentor developers, establish delivery patterns, and help teams use AI responsibly to build and modernize software faster without sacrificing quality, security, or maintainability.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead a team of developers through new application builds and modernization programs while remaining actively involved in design, coding, review, testing, and troubleshooting
  • Set technical direction for projects, including architecture, integration patterns, modernization strategy, engineering standards, delivery approach, and technical risk management
  • Use AI-assisted development tools to accelerate code comprehension, generation, refactoring, testing, documentation, and migration planning while ensuring that outputs are validated by experienced engineering judgment
  • Architect and build fit-for-purpose agents and agentic workflows using frameworks such as LangGraph, A2A, MCP-enabled tools, or comparable technologies
  • Guide modernization of existing applications by analyzing legacy code, identifying business logic, assessing constraints, defining target architecture, and creating incremental transformation roadmaps
  • Make pragmatic architecture decisions across APIs, data models, cloud services, security, observability, integration, DevSecOps, and user experience considerations
  • Mentor developers in software engineering practices, AI-assisted delivery techniques, secure coding, automated testing, maintainable design, and effective code review
  • Collaborate with architects, product owners, business stakeholders, client technical teams, and delivery leaders to translate business needs into executable technical plans
  • Identify and manage risks in AI-generated software, including brittle code, hidden assumptions, weak tests, security issues, licensing concerns, maintainability gaps, and architecture drift
  • Create reusable patterns, accelerators, prompts, agents, reference architectures, and engineering practices that help the broader team deliver modernization work more effectively

Who You Are

You are a senior developer and technical leader who still enjoys building useful software and solving hard problems. You have seen enough delivery challenges to recognize patterns, anticipate risks, and help a team choose the right architecture and engineering approach for the situation.

You have led developers through either new software development projects, application modernization efforts, or both. You know how to establish technical direction, break complex work into deliverable increments, coach developers through tradeoffs, and keep the team focused on building software that is secure, maintainable, testable, and aligned to business outcomes.

You are excited by the changes coming to software development. You have a growth mindset, actively experiment with AI-assisted development tools, and are interested in creating practical agents, workflows, and engineering practices that help teams build, understand, modernize, and operate software more effectively.

Required Technical and Professional Expertise

  • Significant hands-on software development experience delivering production-quality applications
  • Experience leading a team of developers, including mentoring, code review, technical planning, delivery guidance, and issue resolution
  • Experience setting technical direction for software delivery projects, including architecture decisions, engineering standards, delivery patterns, and technical risk management
  • Experience with at least one modern programming language such as Java, Python, JavaScript/TypeScript, C#, Go, or comparable technologies
  • Experience with either new application development, application modernization, or both
  • Practical experience using AI-assisted development tools to support coding, refactoring, testing, documentation, debugging, code comprehension, and architecture exploration
  • Experience reviewing and validating AI-generated code for correctness, security, maintainability, performance, testability, and alignment with architecture and requirements
  • Familiarity with agentic development concepts and experience building or prototyping fit-for-purpose agents using LangGraph, A2A, MCP-enabled tools, or similar frameworks
  • Strong understanding of software architecture and engineering fundamentals, including APIs, data models, integration patterns, automated testing, version control, CI/CD, secure coding, observability, and operational support
  • Ability to analyze existing codebases, identify modernization opportunities, define target-state architecture, and create pragmatic incremental transformation plans
  • Ability to communicate technical direction clearly to developers, architects, stakeholders, and client teams
  • Growth mindset and enthusiasm for how AI will reshape the software development profession

Preferred Technical and Professional Experience

  • Experience modernizing legacy applications, including mainframe, Fortran, J2EE, ASP, monolithic, or other enterprise application estates
  • Experience architecting cloud-native applications, APIs, microservices, event-driven systems, or modern front-end experiences
  • Hands-on experience with LangGraph, A2A, MCP, OpenAI or Anthropic APIs, Semantic Kernel, CrewAI, or comparable agent and orchestration frameworks
  • Experience designing agents that interact with enterprise tools, repositories, documentation, tickets, CI/CD pipelines, runtime telemetry, or application data
  • Experience defining architecture guardrails, reference implementations, coding standards, reusable components, or engineering playbooks for delivery teams
  • Familiarity with DevSecOps practices, automated quality gates, observability, containerization, infrastructure as code, and secure software delivery pipelines
  • Experience with retrieval-augmented generation, vector databases, tool calling, evaluation harnesses, prompt engineering, LLM application testing, or agent observability
  • Experience working in Agile delivery environments with product owners, architects, business stakeholders, client executives, and distributed engineering teams

Ability to mentor and influence other developers in practical, responsible, and effective use of AI-assisted software development practices

raw.excerpt: Staff Product Designer, Guest & DiscoveryCompanyCollaborative Boating operates Boatsetter and GetMyBoat, the two largest marketplaces for getting on the water, now converging into one platform.
raw.description:
Staff Product Designer, Guest & Discovery

Company

Collaborative Boating operates Boatsetter and GetMyBoat, the two largest marketplaces for getting on the water, now converging into one platform. Guests arrive wanting something specific — a fishing trip, a sunset cruise, a birthday on a pontoon — and we connect them to the captains, operators, and owners who can make it happen. Finding and booking a day outside should be as easy and intuitive as booking a flight.

The problem

Search is changing under us. Guests arrive with intent expressed in natural language, increasingly through an AI assistant instead of a search box, and increasingly on a surface we don't own. Answering that with a chatbot is the obvious move and the wrong one: choosing between boats is a parallel, visual, comparison task, and a conversation is sequential. The work is holding both — a visual discovery experience built for comparison, and a compact, structured expression of a listing that holds up when a third-party assistant renders it in a layout we didn't design.

The center of gravity is the search results card. It's the smallest unit of persuasion we have: a handful of facts, ordered, that a guest uses to decide whether to look closer. Which facts earn a place, in what order, and how that adapts from "boat rental Miami" to "something fun for eight people Saturday" — that's the problem. It's an information design problem before it's a visual one.

What you'll own

  • The end-to-end guest discovery experience — search, filtering and refinement, results, map and list, the listing page, and the paths in from organic search and AI assistants. Coherence across both brands and web plus mobile is yours.
  • The information hierarchy of the results card, defended with evidence, across guest intents and every state the data actually produces: missing photos, no reviews yet, a price range instead of a price, partial availability.
  • Interfaces over a system that infers. Make what it inferred legible, make correcting it easy, and reduce verification labor rather than creating it — a guest who has to double-check our answer has been handed our work.
  • Surfaces we don't render. With engineering, shape the structured expression of an experience, an offer, and an operator so it survives being summarized, quoted, or laid out by someone else's assistant.
  • Continuous discovery with your pod — a Product Manager and an engineering tech lead. Choose the cheapest artifact that answers the open question; spend fidelity when a decision is actually being committed.

How we work

Five things worth knowing before you apply. They aren't universal, and here they aren't negotiable.

Problem, then system, then experience

We frame the problem, then settle the shape of the system — entities, states, edge cases — and only then design the experience within it. Your rough exploration runs alongside the system design and improves it; committed fidelity comes later. In practice that means days of useful work before there's a screen worth showing, and arguing about data models with your tech lead while the design is still loose. If you need a settled brief before you can start, this will be frustrating.

Discovery is ongoing, not a handed off spec

You talk to guests and operators directly. You bring opportunities forward rather than receiving them. There's no research team handing you findings and no Product Manager writing you requirements — the pod owns the outcome and you're one third of it. We believe the commercial results follow from understanding these customers better than anyone else does, which is why the understanding isn't delegated to a function.

We ask what moved, not what shipped

You define the signal before release and watch it after. Hitting the number you set is the floor, not the finish — the work worth remembering beat it, and we'd rather you aim at that and miss than aim at the floor and land. Sometimes the answer is that your design didn't work, you say so plainly, and we kill it. If measurement feels like a threat to the craft rather than part of it, this will be a hard place to work.

We ship in days, not quarters

Work goes live the day it's ready — no launch calendar, no approval chain. The pod decides and it goes out. Fast here means small and finished, not big and rough: a narrow slice with its states designed and its accessibility handled, in front of real guests this week, then the next slice. The quality bar doesn't move; the amount of surface you hold before releasing does. What you give up is the reveal — your work is live while it's still incomplete in aggregate, and you correct in the open rather than perfecting behind a curtain. Designers who need to control the whole surface before anyone sees it will find this hard.

We cross lines, and we bet on each other

Titles and team boundaries carry little weight here. You'll be inside the domain model with an engineer, in a support queue reading what operators actually complain about, in a pricing conversation that isn't nominally yours. Ask for help early and give it generously. The standing assumption is that the person next to you is good and worth backing before they've proven it to you — and we expect the same read on you.

We work inside the design system by default; a new pattern has to earn itself against what already exists. WCAG 2.1 AA is an accepted platform standard, not a per-feature negotiation.

What you need to have done

  • Held substantial ownership of search, browse, or discovery in a two-sided marketplace — relevance surfaces, faceted filtering, availability and pricing display, map plus list, comparison.
  • Designed information you can defend. Walk us through a dense comparison surface you built: why each element is there, why it's ordered that way, what you removed, and what removing it cost.
  • Designed over a system that infers, ranks, or predicts — communicating state and confidence in real time, and designing the correction path for when the system is wrong.
  • Formed a point of view on search in an AI-driven world, including where conversation doesn't belong. We'd rather you disagree with us than agree quickly.

What also helps

Fluency with entities, states, and contracts alongside your tech lead. Restraint and typographic craft in high-information surfaces. AI tools in your own practice. Search relevance literacy, structured data and schema work, third-party assistant surfaces, or travel, hospitality, and local-services search at scale are each a plus rather than a requirement.

Your portfolio

Send work, not a slide deck about process. Two or three cases at depth. For at least one: the problem and how you knew it was real, what you tried and abandoned, the hierarchy decisions and their rationale, the states you designed for, what shipped, and what it changed. Include something that didn't work. Roughness is fine — we care about the reasoning.

Practicals

Remote, with high overlap in United States Eastern hours. You'll join a five-person design team, report to our Director of Design, and be the dedicated designer in this pod. Relevant degrees in design, HCI, or information architecture are welcome and not required — portfolio and shipped, measured work outweigh credentials.

About the Role
We are building the next generation of healthcare technology — an AI-native product organization that moves fast, operates with intention, and ships products that meaningfully improve care. The Head of Transformation is a senior operating role that sits at the center of that mission in product.

Reporting directly to the Chief Product Officer, you will serve as a force-multiplier for the CPO — translating vision into operating rhythm, building the connective tissue across product, design, engineering, and the business, and ensuring that the organization's most important bets get the attention, structure, and follow-through they deserve.

The right candidate is equally comfortable writing a strategy memo, facilitating a cross-functional alignment session, designing a planning process from scratch, and rolling up their sleeves to program management a strategic project.

A Day in the Life

CPO Leverage & Office of the CPO

  • Serve as the CPO's thought partner and operational deputy, preparing briefing materials, driving follow-through on key initiatives, and acting as a proxy in select forums.
  • Own the CPO's planning calendar: quarterly business reviews, product leadership offsites, board and executive updates, and annual planning cycles.
  • Distil complex, cross-functional inputs into crisp written recommendations, decision documents, and narratives for senior audiences.
  • Identify issues before they surface to the CPO — proactively resolving blockers, brokering alignment, and escalating only what truly requires executive attention.

Product Operations & Operating Rhythm

  • Design and stand up the product operating model for an AI-native organization — including portfolio prioritization, OKR processes, roadmap governance, and cross-functional rituals.
  • Build lightweight, high-signal reporting cadences that give the CPO and product leadership real-time visibility into progress, risks, and decisions.
  • Drive quarterly and annual planning: coordinating inputs from product, engineering, design, data science, and go-to-market teams into a coherent, executable plan.
  • Identify operational inefficiencies and eliminate them — the goal is a product organization that ships faster and with less friction, not more process.

Transformation & Strategic Initiatives

  • Lead high-priority transformation programs on behalf of the CPO — spanning organizational design, AI adoption, new capability builds, and cross-functional change management.
  • Act as a program manager for initiatives that cut across multiple teams and do not have a natural single owner.
  • Build the infrastructure for how the product organization makes and communicates decisions — from DACI frameworks to async-first working norms.
  • Partner with People, Finance, and Legal as needed to bring structure to people and resource decisions in the product org.

AI-Native Ways of Working

  • Help shape what it means to operate as an AI-native product organization — piloting new tools, workflows, and norms and socializing them across the team.
  • Build muscle around how the product organization consumes, generates, and acts on AI-driven insights.
  • Partner with product and design leadership to embed AI-first thinking into how we scope, prototype, and evaluate work.

What You Need

  • 7–12+ years of experience in product management, strategy, management consulting, chief of staff, or business operations roles — ideally with meaningful time in a high-growth technology or healthcare technology company.
  • Track record of building from scratch. You have stood up new processes, teams, or functions and know how to earn buy-in without authority.
  • Familiarity with AI tooling and modern product operating models. You are curious and opinionated about how AI changes how teams work, and you have practical experience putting AI to use.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication. You can write a crisp one-pager for the CEO and a detailed PRD spec in the same week. You tailor your message to the audience.
  • Strong product intuition. You do not need to be a product manager, but you need to speak the language fluently — roadmaps, trade-offs, customer insight, technical constraints.
  • Structured thinking under ambiguity. You can hold complexity, work through incomplete information, and still drive decisions forward.
  • Genuine comfort as an individual contributor. You are not waiting to manage people. You are energised by the idea of building something from the ground up and rolling up your sleeves.
  • High emotional intelligence and organisational savvy. You build trust quickly, navigate competing priorities with empathy, and know how to influence without creating friction.

We offer competitive benefits to set you up for success in and outside of work.

Here’s What We Offer

  • Generous Paid Time Off: Recharge and relax with 20 days of fixed time off per year, in addition to company holidays—because we believe work-life balance fuels performance.
  • Best-in-Class Parental Leave: Spend quality time with your growing family. We offer one of the industry’s most generous parental leave policies to support you during life’s most important moments.
  • Recognition & Rewards: We celebrate wins—big and small. Get rewarded with monetary incentives and company-wide recognition for your impact and dedication. Your hard work won’t go unnoticed.
  • Comprehensive Insurance Coverage: Stay covered with medical, dental, and vision insurance, plus 100% company-paid short- and long-term disability and basic life insurance. Optional perks include discounted legal aid and pet insurance.

Looking for a Talent Acquisition Specialist to help us connect talented people with the best opportunities! 🚀

💚 About us:

  • We're Huzzle - we connect top talents with leading companies across UK, US, and Europe.
  • Hearty, family-like environment with a close-knit team of 30 working remotely.
  • Mission: Unlocking global opportunity talent people everywhere.
  • Emphasis on autonomy, encouraging each member to act as an entrepreneur within the team.
  • We offer a steep learning curve and a chance to grow your skills rapidly.
  • Ranked 7th fastest-growing company in the UK and 14th fastest in Europe in 2026.
  • Opportunity for growth and promotion if you do well!

About the role

We're hiring a Talent Acquisition Specialist to own a portfolio of client roles from kick-off through to offer accepted. You'll review each role brief, shortlist candidates from our talent database, source directly when needed, run interviews, and partner with our internal delivery and sourcing teams to get roles closed. This is a hands-on, target-driven seat for someone who thrives on ownership and pace.

What you'll do

Own your roles end-to-end

  • Take full ownership of assigned client roles, from reviewing the role brief through to a successful placement.
  • Hit monthly placement targets and keep a healthy pipeline of live roles running at all times.

Match and shortlist candidates

  • Shortlist strong candidates for each role using our internal talent database, AI matching tools, and other sourcing channels.
  • Submit candidates that match the brief within agreed timelines.
  • Flag when the talent pool is exhausted and request extra sourcing support.

Source, interview & post jobs

  • Source candidates directly via LinkedIn Recruiter, your own network, and other channels when the talent pool is thin or the role is niche.
  • Interview candidates yourself when you need to confirm fit, verify experience, or fill gaps left by upstream screening.
  • Create and manage job ads on our ATS and external job boards when a role needs dedicated outreach.

Calibrate with clients and move roles forward

  • Work with the delivery manager and operations team to calibrate candidates against client requirements.
  • Take client feedback and use it to refine the brief and keep roles progressing.
  • Push back on unrealistic or unfillable briefs rather than carrying dead roles.

Collaborate across the team

  • Partner with the delivery, sourcing, and account management teams to keep every role progressing efficiently.
  • Contribute to team conversations on process, quality, and candidate fit.

Keep your data clean

  • Keep role status, candidate records, role briefs, and pipeline data accurate and up to date in our internal systems at all times.
  • Surface process issues and suggest improvements when you spot them.

How success is measured

  • Monthly placements against target.
  • Pipeline health: number of active roles, time-to-submit, time-to-fill.
  • Submission quality — client interview and offer rates per submission.
  • Data accuracy across the ATS and internal systems.

Requirements

  • 3–6+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience, ideally in agency, RPO, or a high-volume in-house environment.
  • A track record of hitting placement or fill targets and managing a live pipeline of open roles.
  • Confident direct sourcer — fluent with LinkedIn Recruiter, Boolean search, and creative outbound.
  • Comfortable running candidate interviews and making your own call on whether someone fits the brief.
  • Strong client and stakeholder skills, including the confidence to push back on unrealistic briefs with evidence.
  • Disciplined operator — keeps ATS, CRM, and pipeline data clean without being chased.
  • Comfortable working with AI-powered matching and sourcing tools.

Nice to have

  • Experience recruiting across multiple functions or geographies.
  • Background in a marketplace, staffing platform, or fast-scaling startup.
  • Familiarity with modern ATS platforms and recruiting automation stacks.

Benefits

We offer a competitive base salary plus an uncapped monthly commission paid on the value of each placement (the fee Huzzle invoices the client). Commission is paid monthly in arrears on placements that complete in the previous month, with the rate stepping up as you hit and exceed your monthly target.

Over time, the organization has become one of the largest players in the medical space, reaching nearly 50% of prospective medical students every year through one of our products or services.

Working at MedSchoolCoach

We are a distributed team of creative, approachable, and motivated entrepreneurs, educators, tutors, advisors, and clinicians who are passionate about improving healthcare and education. At MedSchoolCoach, we value problem solvers who take initiative, communicate earnestly, work effectively, and prioritize life-work balance. We do everything we can to make sure our teammates are successful personally and professionally. We welcome all employee contributions in whatever shape or form they manifest, especially as our organization continues to grow.

About the Role

We are looking for individuals who have a passion for education and helping students applying to medical school. Working together with a physician advisor, the writing advisor will support medical school applicants through the application process in the form of helping the applicant draft, revise, and edit the personal statement, activities section, and secondary applications, among other materials. The goal is to provide polished documents that are compelling and representative of the applicant.

Scope

  • Develop a strong working relationship with the physician advisor, acting as a unified team that will support the applicant through the application process
  • Assist the applicant in restructuring content and ensuring responses and essays have a logical and cohesive flow
  • Provide suggestions and guiding questions that enable the applicant to develop content
  • Edit materials for clarity, tone, and syntax
  • Proofread materials for grammar and word choice
  • Answer questions about the writing process for specific materials
  • Provide relevant and actionable feedback
  • Maintain a supportive environment for the applicant

Most of the application materials that you will work on will require two or three revisions. The personal statement can be up to 5,300 characters. The activities section consists of 15 entries, with each one having a maximum limit of 700 characters. In addition to the 15 entries, the activities sections allows three activities to be noted as the applicant’s “most meaningful” allowing the applicant to provide a response regarding their reasoning for this choice (1,500 characters, maximum). A secondary application can include 1-12 prompts with varying word count limits. The average response is 1-2 paragraphs. Many of our clients purchase packages that include assistance for five or 20 secondary applications. Clients may occasionally need editing services for other applications materials.

This is, largely, a seasonal position. Our peak season is from March until September. We expect that our advisors have consistent availability during this time. Also, this is a remote position that requires you to have a reliable connection to the Internet and access to Microsoft Word.

Ideal Candidate

  • a BA and an MA in the humanities or “writing-heavy” major (additional professional experience may be substituted for an MA)
  • a combination of the following professional experiences:
    • 2+ years of experience in education. This can include university teaching/working as a teaching assistant (especially for a writing program or humanities course), grades 9-12 teaching (ELA), tutoring (ELA, writing), working as a paraprofessional or instructional assistant in K-12 education, and ELA curriculum development.
    • 2+ years in a writing-heavy role. This can include editing, grant writing, journalist roles, and content writing, among others.
  • a combination of the following behavioral characteristics:
    • Natural teacher/guide
    • Natural teacher/guide
    • Compassionate
    • Patient
    • Curious
    • Passionate about writing
    • Flexible/adaptable
    • Seeks professional development
    • Open and responsive to feedback
    • Team player
    • Promotes diversity and inclusion

raw.description:
The Mission

Voyagu is a travel operations platform, a large product that powers travel agencies end to end — trip economics, sales, ticketing, accounting and marketing — with a wide range of integrations with GDS and external services (payments, email, calls/SMS and more). Many kinds of users work inside it, from agents and searchers to back-office teams, and the agencies’ own clients interact with the platform through a separate web interface.

We're hiring a Feature Engineer, who owns features end to end and drives an AI agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex) as a daily engineering tool.

The Bet We're Making

We bet on speed of thinking and quality of work with an agent, not years of stack. We want an engineer who, with an AI agent, ships like a stronger engineer — because they lead the agent instead of clicking "accept."

You write a plan, break work into steps, verify each step, reason about the output, and give precise next instructions. You don't trust code you haven't verified. If your style is "generate it and click around the UI until it seems to work," this isn't for you — and vice versa.

You Care Why, Not Just How

You engage with the business problem, not just the ticket. You don't need to know travel — the domain is specific and nobody arrives knowing it. What matters is that you get curious about why a feature exists, who needs it, and what changes once it ships. When a business stakeholder comes to you, that conversation is interesting, not an interruption. That habit is a large part of what we're selecting for.

Tech Stack

  • Backend: Python (SQLAlchemy, GraphQL, PostgreSQL) — complex queries against a rich data model. Writing complex SQL itself is something an agent helps with. The judgment around it is on you.
  • Frontend: Angular — kept deliberately thin, with help available for the harder parts. You don’t need to be a frontend expert, just the kind of person who says “I’ll take the feature,” not “that’s not my layer.”
  • Agent: Claude Code / Cursor / Codex as a normal, daily tool (your choice of agent).

What You'll Do

  • Own features end to end across the platform: economics, sales, ticketing, integrations and more.
  • Build services in Python (SQLAlchemy, GraphQL, PostgreSQL) with correct transactional behavior.
  • Integrate external systems: GDS, payments, email, calls/SMS and other services.
  • Ship the full slice of a feature, including the Angular frontend when it needs it.
  • Work with an AI agent daily — plan, steps, verification — owning quality, not volume of generated lines.
  • Grow scope fast as the team and responsibilities expand.

What We're Looking For

  • Solid backend development experience in Python.
  • Strong understanding of database transactions and data correctness; comfortable with complex queries (mandatory).
  • Real, daily experience working with an AI agent (Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or similar) — a requirement, not a plus.
  • A disciplined process: planning, step-by-step work, verifying your own code.
  • Genuine interest in the business behind the code — you can explain what problem a feature solved and who it served.
  • Willingness and ability to work across the stack, including frontend. You own features, not layers.
  • English B2+ (working level).

Why Voyagu

  • A large, real product — a travel operations platform with many domains, so you get variety and depth, not one narrow corner.
  • An AI-first engineering culture: the agent is the norm, not a banned tool.
  • Fast-growing responsibility for people who deliver.
  • Fully remote, start ASAP.

Our client, an international e-commerce company with a strong presence in the USA, is seeking a detail-oriented and proactive Inventory & Logistics Specialist to oversee end-to-end supply chain and inventory operations. This full-time remote role combines freight management, Amazon FBA coordination, inventory forecasting, and reverse logistics to ensure smooth operations across all sales channels. If you are experienced in e-commerce logistics, Amazon fulfillment, and supply chain optimization, and enjoy working in a fast-paced, high-impact environment, wed love to hear from you.

About the company:

The company is a premium pet brand known for its high-quality, durable bulky pet products and accessories. Built for both professionals and devoted pet owners, the brands products are designed with attention to detail, functionality, and longevity. The brand is committed to creating elevated, practical experiences for pets and their people—and is looking for an Inventory & Logistics Specialist to help scale that mission by ensuring seamless product flow from factory to customer.

Key Responsibilities:

Freight & Supply Chain Management

  • Manage end-to-end order placement with factories and track order progress through to completion.
  • Request, negotiate, and select the best quotes from freight forwarders, determining the optimal type of sea freight for each specific situation.
  • Design ideal loading configurations for shipping containers based on product dimensions to maximize space and reduce shipping costs.
  • Oversee the loading process through active communication with factories and freight partners.
  • Track all global shipments, proactively flagging and mitigating any potential delays.

Amazon FBA & E-commerce Operations

  • Create and manage Amazon Shipments, utilizing software solutions (e.g., 9Yards and similar simulation tools) to run multiple simulations and target the most cost-effective Amazon warehouses.
  • Oversee the receiving of units at both Amazon fulfillment centers and partner 3PL warehouses.
  • Perform thorough reconciliation for all inbound shipments to ensure accurate stock levels and file claims for missing units when necessary.
  • Coordinate Less-Than-Truckload (LTL) orders for Last Mile transport from our 3PL to customers for non-Amazon (DTC/B2B) orders.

Inventory Forecasting & Management

  • Continuously monitor inventory levels across all sales channels to prevent overstocking or Out-of-Stock (OOS) situations.
  • Forecast inventory movements and project OOS dates at the SKU level to accurately plan factory order quantities.

Reverse Logistics & Returns Management

  • Create and manage Amazon removal orders for customer returns.
  • Arrange transport from Amazon to 3PL/processing facilities.
  • Oversee the de-kitting, inspection, and sorting of damaged units into tiers for parts harvesting or resale.

Scale of Operations:

  • Container Shipments: ~8 per month.
  • LTL Orders (Last Mile): ~10 per week.
  • Factory Orders: ~6 per year.

Software & Workflow Proficiency:

  • Amazon FBA & E-commerce Systems: Deep expertise with Amazon Seller Central, FBA placement optimization, inbound reconciliation, and removal/disposal orders.
  • Forecasting & Inventory Management: Hands-on experience with IMS tools (SoStocked, RestockPro, Cin7, Skubana), advanced Excel or Google Sheets for SKU-level forecasting and run-rate models.
  • Logistics, Freight & 3PL Integration: Familiarity with container load planning software (EasyCargo, CubeMaster), freight platforms (Flexport, Freightos), warehouse management systems (ShipStation, ShipHero), and reverse logistics workflows.

Core Competencies

  • 3+ years of experience in supply chain, logistics, or Amazon inventory management.
  • Proven ability to manage complex shipments and multi-stage fulfillment workflows across international markets.
  • Strong understanding of Amazon FBA processes and multi-channel e-commerce operations.
  • Advanced analytical mindset with the ability to build and interpret detailed SKU-level forecasting and inventory models.
  • Practical experience coordinating international freight, container shipments, and 3PL operations in a multi-channel environment.
  • Strong problem-solving skills and high attention to detail.
  • Ability to work independently while coordinating with multiple stakeholders.
  • Alignment with the companys premium brand standards and operational excellence mindset.

Why Join Us:

  • Play a critical role in ensuring smooth operations for a high-ticket pet brand on Amazon.
  • Own inventory planning, logistics, and fulfillment workflows.
  • Work remotely from anywhere.
  • Competitive salary and flexible working hours.
  • Collaborate with a creative, forward-thinking team dedicated to innovation in the pet space.

What You’ll Do

  • work with our CRO team when deeper strategy is needed

This is not primarily a prospecting role.We’re building the acquisition engine to keep our closers busy. You may help with other sales activities while ramping, but your main responsibility is closing.

What You Bring

  • 2+ years of B2B sales experience
  • proven experience closing deals, not just setting appointments
  • agency sales experience OR experience selling an eCommerce-focused B2B offer
  • experience selling to founders and senior decision-makers
  • strong discovery, objection handling, follow-up, and closing skills
  • excellent spoken and written English
  • strong understanding of eCommerce and DTC businesses
  • confidence discussing revenue, conversion rates, marketing, and growth
  • a track record of hitting sales targets
  • strong ownership over your pipeline and results

Bonus points for:

  • experience selling CRO, Shopify development, web design, paid media, or other agency services
  • experience selling $5k–$15k+ offers
  • experience selling recurring retainers
  • deep Shopify / DTC knowledge

Qualified Call VolumeOur bottleneck is sales capacity, not acquisition. Once ramped, our goal is to give you 6–8 qualified calls per day.

A Strong ProductYou’ll sell CRO services that create measurable value for our clients, backed by real results and case studies.

Real OwnershipYou own your calls, pipeline, follow-ups, and results. We give you room to perform.

Leadership OpportunityWe’re building a team of 2–3 closers. Top performers will have opportunities to grow into sales leadership as Fuelerate scales.

  • handle multiple calls per day

Remote, Europe, Full-time, Director, 6-8 years of experience

Who We Are

At Yuno, we are building the payment infrastructure that allows all companies to participate in the global market. Founded by seasoned experts from the payments and tech industries, our technology provides access to leading payment capabilities, enabling companies to engage customers confidently and maintain global operations through seamless integrations.

We empower high-performing teams at brands like InDrive, McDonald’s, Rappi, and Viva Aerobus to integrate 1,000+ payment methods through a single API. By leveraging advanced AI and the latest technologies, we orchestrate smart routing and fraud prevention across 80+ countries.

About The Role

We are looking for a commercially minded lawyer to join our global Legal and Compliance team as Legal Business Partner for EMEA. You will work closely with our commercial, partnerships, and operations teams across Europe, the Middle East, and Asia, providing practical legal support that enables the business to move forward with confidence. At Yuno, Legal and Compliance operate as business partners, and you will count on the support and playbooks of the global team. The role is remote and can be based anywhere in the region.

Your contribution will be

  • Business partnering: Serve as the primary legal counterpart for the EMEA commercial, partnerships, and operations teams, providing pragmatic, business-oriented advice.

  • Contract negotiation and drafting: Negotiate and draft merchant, partner, and vendor agreements across the region, applying and helping improve our global contracting playbooks.

  • Regulatory support: Advise the business on payments regulation and data protection across the region, in coordination with the global Legal and Compliance team, and help maintain Yuno’s positioning as a technology orchestration layer that does not hold funds.

  • Corporate and entity support: Support the corporate maintenance of Yuno’s entities in the region, working with the global team, outside counsel, and corporate service providers.

  • Growth and expansion: Provide legal guidance on new markets, new products, and strategic partnerships as Yuno continues to grow across the region.

Skills You Need

Minimum Qualifications

  • Law degree and qualification in at least one jurisdiction within the region.

  • 6-8 years of experience across law firm and in-house roles; payments, fintech, or technology experience strongly preferred.

  • Strong commercial contracts and negotiation skills; familiarity with European payments regulation and GDPR, with Middle East or Asia exposure a plus.

  • A business enablement mindset: a practical approach to risk and the ability to deliver clear, actionable advice.

  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced, high-growth environment, working across time zones with a globally distributed team.

  • Fluency in English; other regional languages are a plus.

What We Offer at Yuno

  • Competitive Compensation

raw.description:
At Limitlessli, we specialize in recruiting, hiring, and managing high-caliber remote staff for dynamic and growing healthcare facilities. Leveraging our extensive global network, we connect clients with highly qualified professionals, offering meticulously tailored services to meet our clients' unique business needs.

The Opportunity:

We are looking for a highly analytical and detail-oriented Forensic Utility Bill Auditor / Data Analyst to join our team. In this role, you will review and analyze utility accounts—including gas, electric, and water—to identify billing errors, incorrect rate classifications, tariff misapplications, unusual usage patterns, and potential overcharges.

You will work with utility bills, customer portals, spreadsheets, AI-powered data extraction tools, and public property information to investigate anomalies and help build evidence supporting potential audit findings and recovery claims.

This position is remote and offers you the flexibility of working from home.

Your responsibilities will include:

  • Review customer utility accounts and billing histories to identify high-value accounts requiring further investigation.
  • Download and organize historical utility bills and supporting documentation.
  • Prepare clear, accurate, and professional communications to utility providers outlining identified billing discrepancies, suspected errors, and supporting findings for further investigation and resolution.
  • Create and maintain standardized folder structures and audit files for each client, utility type, account, or property.
  • Prioritize accounts based on billing thresholds and potential financial impact.
  • Standardize utility statements into clean, readable PDFs suitable for data extraction and analysis.
  • Use AI-powered tools to extract up to 24 months of utility billing data into structured spreadsheets.
  • Analyze billing information using Month-over-Month (MoM) and Year-over-Year (YoY) comparisons.
  • Review key data points, including:
    • Billing cycle dates
    • Total monthly charges
    • Energy or utility consumption
    • Rates and tariffs
    • Meter types and rate classes
    • Itemized charges, including generation, transmission, and delivery costs
  • Identify irregular usage patterns, billing anomalies, potentially unjustified charges, and other indicators of possible overbilling.
  • Perform detailed quality assurance by manually validating AI-generated data against the original utility bills.
  • Research property characteristics, including square footage, property type, and visible operational factors that may impact utility usage.
  • Prepare targeted questions for clients to better understand property operations and consumption patterns.
  • Investigate suspected billing errors, including incorrect rate classes, meter types, and tariff violations.
  • Support the calculation of potential historical overcharges and assist in documenting the evidence behind audit findings.
  • Independently verify utility tariffs, rate schedules, regulations, and other supporting documentation using official published sources before finalizing findings.
  • Manage multiple high-priority accounts simultaneously while maintaining accuracy, organization, and attention to detail.

The role requires a combination of data extraction, benchmarking, manual quality assurance, property research, and tariff validation.

Qualifications & Experience Required:

  • Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Data Analytics, Business, Engineering, Energy Management, or a related field is preferred.
  • Previous experience in data analysis, auditing, utility billing, energy management, financial analysis, or forensic analysis is highly desirable.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to identify patterns, anomalies, discrepancies, and potential errors within large sets of financial and operational data.
  • Excellent written communication skills.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets, including data organization, calculations, comparisons, and analysis.
  • Experience working with large volumes of documents and maintaining highly organized digital filing systems.
  • Familiarity with AI-powered data extraction or document analysis tools is an advantage.
  • Experience reviewing utility bills, tariffs, rate schedules, meter types, or energy consumption data is preferred.
  • Strong research skills and the ability to locate and interpret information from official utility, regulatory, and public sources.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and a commitment to manually verifying data accuracy.
  • Ability to understand and compare Month-over-Month and Year-over-Year performance and identify unusual variances.
  • Strong problem-solving and investigative skills, with the ability to determine the potential cause of discrepancies.
  • Comfortable managing multiple accounts and priorities simultaneously.
  • A high level of integrity, accuracy, and discretion when handling client financial and operational information.

Service Fee:

Industry standards applicable to the state depending on work experience and level of expertise.

Hours:

US Eastern Standard Time (EST) - 10am to 6pm

Why Limitlessli?

We embrace the flexibility and convenience of a remote working environment, and you will collaborate with an international team while contributing to our growing business, all from the comfort of your home.

You will need to have some essential tools – a reliable computer and noise-canceling headset, a second monitor for enhanced productivity, and a stable internet connection. You’ll also be required to have a backup internet connection, ensuring that you’re well-equipped to complete your work seamlessly.
